title: South Carolina's measles outbreak jumped to Washington state 5 times in 2 weeks
gist: A NEJM Evidence study shows South Carolina's measles outbreak seeded Washington state five separate times in two weeks (26 resident cases), underlining that domestic travel and under-vaccinated communities, not imports, now drive US measles.

insights.claim: Genome sequencing showed Washington's January cases came from five distinct importations from South Carolina rather than one introduction, leading to 26 resident cases.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Whole-genome sequencing is a decisive tool in separating importation from local spread.
insights.quote: timely whole-genome sequencing can supplement epidemiologic information to help differentiate distinct importations from local transmission

insights.claim: Two of the five importations produced clusters (14 and 7 cases) after infectious people visited schools, healthcare facilities and a church; the others produced zero or one secondary case.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Outbreak size is driven by exposures in schools and clinics, a lever for public-health response.

insights.claim: Officials credit basic quarantine, isolation and contact tracing for stopping wider spread.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Low-tech response capacity still works; erosion of public-health staffing would raise outbreak risk.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning "Officials credit basic public health"

insights.claim: South Carolina's outbreak ran Oct 2, 2025 to Apr 26, 2026 with 997 cases, the largest since elimination until Pennsylvania's ongoing outbreak surpassed it.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Outbreaks are getting bigger and more frequent as vaccination slips.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning "South Carolina's measles outbreak began"

insights.claim: Domestic travel now poses a greater measles risk than international imports as vaccination rates slip.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Outbreak risk is spreading with ordinary domestic mobility; relevant for schools and healthcare capacity planning.

insights.claim: CDC data show only 18 of 4,588 confirmed US measles cases this year came from international visitors, while 4,404 (96 percent) link to a domestic outbreak, with 43 new outbreaks.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
insights.so_what: The case load is homegrown and tied to under-vaccinated communities.

insights.claim: The study contradicts HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s claims of a 'global outbreak' and that the US is controlling measles better than any country; the author calls both claims false.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
insights.so_what: Political friction over vaccine policy may shape public-health funding and vaccine-related policy risk.

top_entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
